core.title: Reference color tokens instead of raw color literals in UI files
core.given: A repository that has a design-system root (profile: roots.design_system), and a UI artifact anywhere in that repository — inside or outside the root — outside the design-token layer (profile: layout.locations#design_token_layer), of a kind the profile counts as UI (profile: roles.presentation.kinds)
core.when: A color is written in a styled value of that artifact (a style declaration, inline style, style block, style object, or color-setting presentation attribute — profile: idiom.design_system#color_value_contexts)
core.then: Define the required color once in the design-token layer and reference that token from UI code by the stack's token-reference syntax (profile: idiom.design_system#token_reference); never write a raw color literal (profile: idiom.design_system#raw_color_literal) in the value.
prefer: During GREEN: reuse an existing semantic color token when it already expresses the required role.
During GREEN: add the smallest new semantic token only when the current visual behavior needs a distinct value.
During GREEN: change only the affected UI reference.
avoid: Do not broaden: retheming unrelated components.
Do not broaden: duplicating an existing token under a new name.
Do not broaden: using a raw literal as a temporary shortcut.
unless: Token definitions (the stack's token-definition syntax, profile: idiom.design_system#token_definition) define tokens wherever they live and are not flagged.
Named colors and reserved color keywords (such as the transparent and current-color keywords) are not raw color literals and are not flagged.
core.why: A raw color is a theme decision made in one place: it does not follow dark mode, drifts from the palette, and nobody can find it when the palette changes.
evidence: The current visual or behavioral acceptance passes.
Affected UI artifacts contain no raw color literal outside the design-token layer (the stack's design-token check reports no finding).
verification: Disposition strict: a finding is not waivable in the task; severity 2.

The check reads styled values in the contexts the profile lists (profile: idiom.design_system#color_value_contexts) — style declarations, inline styles, style blocks, style objects, color-setting presentation attributes, and markup authored in string literals — and flags raw color literals (profile: idiom.design_system#raw_color_literal) in their values.
Selectors are not values: color-like text in a selector position is never read as a color.

Self-scoping: the rule applies only when the repository has a design-system root (profile: roots.design_system); with none, the repository is not judged — there is no system to connect to yet. When the root exists, UI artifacts anywhere in the repository are judged. Detecting the design root needs a repository-tree observer; it is not observable from the touched artifact alone.
The design-token layer (profile: layout.locations#design_token_layer) is where raw colors are defined and is not scanned.

Test artifacts (profile: suffix.unit_test) and the stack's never-scanned vendored/build trees (profile: roots.excluded) are never scanned; the exact classification of which trees count as vendored/build is owned by this rule's checker and is not part of the profile value.
Token definitions (profile: idiom.design_system#token_definition) are not flagged anywhere; named colors and reserved color keywords are not flagged.

In artifacts that author markup inside string literals, only literal text is judged: code, comments and regex literals are never read as declarations, and a value spanning an interpolation is judged on its literal chunks alone.

values: a UI artifact kind (profile: roles.presentation.kinds): markup, stylesheet or component artifact — source artifacts count only for the markup they author in string literals
the UI artifact sits outside the design-token layer (profile: layout.locations#design_token_layer) — in any other layer of the design system, or outside the design root entirely
a raw color literal (profile: idiom.design_system#raw_color_literal) written in a styled value (profile: idiom.design_system#color_value_contexts)

fires: A component artifact outside the design root sets an inline style color to a raw literal while the repository has a design root.
A stylesheet in a non-token layer of the design root declares a translucent raw color in a declaration value.
A source artifact renders markup from a string literal whose inline style or style block contains a raw color literal.
A markup artifact sets a color-setting presentation attribute to a raw color literal.
doesNotFire: The repository has no design-system root.
The raw color is in the design-token layer.
The raw color is itself a token definition (it defines the token wherever it lives).
The value is a named color or a reserved color keyword (transparent, the current-color keyword).
The artifact is a test artifact or lives in a never-scanned vendored/build tree.
Color-like text in a selector position, or inside code, comments or regex literals of a source artifact.

profileRequirements.meaning: Whether and where the repository has a design-system root; its absence self-scopes the rule out entirely, and its presence extends the rule to UI artifacts outside the root.
profileRequirements.bunValue: repository contains a directory matching **/design/, **/design_system/, **/design-system/ — a directory named `design`, `design_system`, or `design-system`

profileRequirements.meaning: Which layer beneath the design root defines design tokens (raw colors) and is therefore exempt from the no-raw-color check, versus the other design layers that must reference tokens.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the first directory beneath the design root names the layer: `tokens` or `foundations`, `primitives`, `components`, `templates`; the tokens/foundations layer is where raw colors are defined and is not scanned

profileRequirements.meaning: Which concrete artifact kinds count as UI artifacts subject to the rule, including source artifacts that author markup in string literals.
profileRequirements.bunValue: .tsx, .jsx, .html, .htm, .css, .ts, .mts — .ts/.mts only count for HTML they author in string/template/tagged-template literals

profileRequirements.meaning: What counts as a raw color literal in the stack's styling syntax (and, by complement, which named or reserved values are not raw).
profileRequirements.bunValue: a hex (`#rgb`/`#rrggbb`/`#rrggbbaa`), `rgb()`/`rgba()`, or `hsl()`/`hsla()` color written in a declaration value; named colors (`red`, `white`) and `currentColor`/`transparent` are not flagged

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete contexts in a UI artifact where a color value can be written and is read by the check.
profileRequirements.bunValue: CSS declarations, `style` attributes, `<style>` blocks, JSX `style={{…}}` objects, `fill`/`stroke`/`bgcolor` attributes in .tsx, .jsx, .html, .htm, .css; plus inline `style="…"` attributes and `<style>` text in HTML a .ts/.mts file renders from string/template/tagged-template literals

profileRequirements.meaning: The syntax by which UI code references a design token instead of writing a raw value.
The syntax by which a design token is defined (a color value bound to a token name); such definitions are exempt wherever they live.
profileRequirements.bunValue: custom property definitions (`--name: <color>`), e.g. `--danger: #b91c1c`, define tokens wherever they live and are not flagged

profileRequirements.meaning: Test-artifact name patterns that are never scanned by the check.

The single stack-wide list of vendored and generated trees that are never scanned by convention checks; this rule reads that list (which trees count as vendored/build is decided by the checker in its own verification, not stored in this profile value).

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (define colors once in the token layer, reference tokens, never raw color literals in UI styled values) is fully stack-neutral; every concrete styling construct is bound through six proposed idiom/layout keys, since the closed vocabulary has no styling or design-system keys. roots.excluded is used only as vocabulary v2 defines it — the single stack-wide list of never-scanned vendored/generated trees (Bun value: vendored/build directories) — and this rule's checker-owned exact classification of those trees stays in core:verification, not in the profile value. Two things could not be made neutral as-is: (1) the repository-level design-root-exists activation fact is not expressible in the neutral fact vocabulary (role/operation/change/phase/finding/file_kind/task_term/task_has_acceptance), so the core carries it in given, in the self-scoping verification entry — preserving its needs_new_observer character — and in doesNotFire[0], with the directory names supplied by profile:roots.design_system; (2) the detector id bun_design_system_detector (evidence[1], activation.facts[3] note) stays bunOnly per the notProfileKeys rule; per-rule severity 2 and disposition strict are core verification, not profile keys. Selector-vs-value and literal-chunks-only judgments are phrased generically (they are properties of style languages and string literals, not of one stack); the Bun sidecar remains the worked example with the concrete CSS/JSX constructs.
